full_text_en:
Changle City Water Supply Company v. Wusi Sub-branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China — dispute over loan guarantee

Ruling Summary

1. A guarantor that holds a business license for a legal person enterprise and is a for-profit enterprise legal person, even if its business operations have certain public service characteristics, is not a public institution for public interest purposes.

2. A guarantor, as a legal person with full civil capacity, shall independently bear civil liability for its civil legal acts in accordance with the law. Whether its guarantee is influenced by a third party outside the contract does not involve the rights and obligations between the parties to the contract and does not affect the validity of the guarantee contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 262

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Changle City Water Supply Company. Domicile: No. 1 Park Road, Chengguan, Changle City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Shanlong, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Weiliang, lawyer of Fujian Zhongmei Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hui, lawyer of Beijing Saidetianqin Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Wusi Sub-branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Fuzhou. Domicile: No. 162 Wusi Road, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province.

Responsible Person: Lin Rongfeng, President of the Sub-branch.

Agent ad litem: Xu Xiaojiang, lawyer of Fujian Zhili Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lin Xi, lawyer of Fujian Zhili Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Heshun (China) Industrial Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Industrial Zone, Zhanggang Town, Changle City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Shunli, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

The appellant Changle City Water Supply Company (hereinafter referred to as Water Supply Company) appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2004) Min Min Chu Zi No. 47 rendered by the High People's Court of Fujian Province in a dispute over a loan guarantee with the respondent Wusi Sub-branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Fuzhou (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Wusi Sub-branch) and the defendant at first instance Heshun (China) Industrial Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Heshun Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Jiang Wei as presiding judge, and Acting Judges Chen Bailing and Yang Zhengyu as members, to hear this case, with Clerk Yuan Hongxia keeping the record. This case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found: On August 29, 2003, Heshun Company borrowed money from ICBC Wusi Sub-branch, and both parties entered into the "Working Capital Loan Contract" No. 2003 (Wusi) ICBC (Short) General Zi No. 13, for an amount of RMB 28,000,000, with a loan maturity date of August 20, 2004, and a monthly interest rate of 4.8675‰, calculated daily and settled monthly. In the event of other serious breaches, ICBC Wusi Sub-branch had the right to terminate the contract and demand that Heshun Company repay the loan principal and interest in advance, and compensate for losses. On the same day, Water Supply Company and ICBC Wusi Sub-branch entered into a "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contract" No. 2003 (Wusi) ICBC (Short) General Zi No. 13 Bao 001 Fen Hao, under which Water Supply Company provided joint and several guarantee for the RMB 28,000,000 loan of Heshun Company in this case. On September 5, 2003, ICBC Wusi Sub-branch disbursed the RMB 28,000,000 loan to Heshun Company. Heshun Company began to default on interest from September 20, 2003, and has not paid any interest to date.

On July 28, 2004, ICBC Wusi Sub-branch filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting a judgment: 1. Ordering Heshun Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 28,000,000 and interest and penalty interest under Contract No. 2003 (Wusi) ICBC (Short) General Zi No. 13 in a lump sum, with interest and penalty interest calculated in accordance with the contract and the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China; 2. Ordering Water Supply Company to assume joint and several liability for repayment of the above debts of Heshun Company; 3. Ordering the two defendants to jointly bear the litigation costs and other related expenses of this case.

After trial, the court of first instance held: The loan contract signed between ICBC Wusi Sub-branch and Heshun Company, and the guarantee contract signed between ICBC Wusi Sub-branch and Water Supply Company, represented the true intentions of the parties, their contents did not violate legal provisions, and they should be recognized as valid contracts. Water Supply Company's defense that it was a state-owned unit of a public welfare nature, did not qualify as a guarantor, the guarantee was coerced by the government, the guarantee was invalid, and it should not bear the guarantee liability, could not be sustained. First, the guarantee contract in this case had been continuously in effect since 1997. Water Supply Company, as an enterprise, enjoyed the autonomy of business operations and had full ability to refuse the guarantee. However, it never raised any objection to the so-called "order" of the government until this lawsuit, but instead repeatedly provided guarantees for Heshun Company's continuous borrowing, thereby waiving the right granted by Article 11 of the Security Law to "refuse to provide guarantees for others when compelled by banks or other financial institutions or enterprises." The evidence submitted was also insufficient to establish that it provided the guarantee under duress. Second, Water Supply Company is a local state-owned enterprise. When its assets are used to provide guarantees for others' loans, approval by the municipal government, relevant superior department leaders, or coordination and instructions by relevant departments and leaders does not violate relevant legal provisions. Such guarantee act neither contravenes its true intention nor falls within the invalid circumstances stipulated in the Security Law. The Supreme People's Court's Notice Fa (1998) No. 85 "On Correctly Determining the Validity of Guarantee Contracts in Enterprise Loan Contract Disputes" also holds that, except where the guarantee contract is indeed in violation of the Security Law and relevant judicial interpretations and should be legally determined invalid, the invalidity of the guarantee contract should not be confirmed solely on the ground that the guarantor's guarantee was contrary to the guarantor's will due to a directive of the local government, and the guarantor should not be relieved of guarantee liability on this ground. Third, Water Supply Company holds a business license for a legal person enterprise and is a for-profit enterprise legal person, not a "public institution for public interest purposes" within the meaning of Article 3 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Security Law, and its guarantee act should not be governed by that provision. Although Water Supply Company's business operations have a public welfare component, in accordance with the spirit of Article 16 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Security Law, which provides that "if a public institution or social organization engaged in business activities acts as a guarantor, the guarantee contract signed shall be deemed valid unless there are other circumstances that render the guarantee contract invalid," the guarantee contract signed by Water Supply Company does not have any other circumstances that would render it invalid, and the guarantee contract it signed should also be deemed valid. In summary, the guarantee contract in this case represented the true intentions of both parties and did not violate relevant legal provisions; it should be recognized as a valid contract, and Water Supply Company should assume the guarantee liability in accordance with the contract. Water Supply Company's argument that the guarantee contract violated legal provisions and should be invalid could not be sustained and should be dismissed. Heshun Company, having been lawfully summoned by the court, failed to appear in court, which was deemed as waiving its right to defend. The court, in accordance with Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 6 and 21 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 130 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, entered the following judgment: 1. Heshun Company shall, within ten days of the effective date of this judgment, repay ICBC Wusi Sub-branch the loan principal of RMB 28,000,000 and the interest and penalty interest as stipulated in the contract, with interest and penalty interest calculated in accordance with the contract and the provisions of the People's Bank of China up to the date of payment determined by this judgment, and any delay shall be penalized in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; 2. Water Supply Company shall bear joint and several liability for the payment under the first item of this judgment. The case acceptance fee of RMB 160,098 and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 125,520 shall be borne by Heshun Company, with Water Supply Company bearing joint and several liability.

Water Supply Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing: Water Supply Company's provision of joint and several liability guarantee for Heshun Company's loan debt was compelled under the mandatory directives of the Changle City government and other administrative organs, and such guarantee act was contrary to Water Supply Company's true intentions and should be deemed invalid. The first instance judgment's finding that Water Supply Company was not a "public institution for public interest purposes" was erroneous. This case may involve economic crimes and should be stayed. The shareholder of the borrower Heshun Company, Hong Kong Shunkai (Group) Co., Ltd., failed to fully pay its registered capital, and it should be added to participate in this lawsuit. It requested the court of second instance to set aside the first instance judgment, amend it to find the guarantee contract invalid, and hold that Water Supply Company should not bear guarantee liability.

In response to Water Supply Company's appeal requests and reasons, ICBC Wusi Sub-branch argued: Water Supply Company's claim that the guarantee contract was entered into against its true intention under the directive of the Changle City government was not supported by sufficient evidence. According to the Supreme People's Court's Notice Fa (1998) No. 85 "On Correctly Determining the Validity of Guarantee Contracts in Enterprise Loan Contract Disputes," except where the guarantee contract is indeed in violation of the Security Law and relevant judicial interpretations and should be legally determined invalid, the invalidity of the guarantee contract should not be confirmed solely on the ground that the guarantor's guarantee was contrary to the guarantor's will due to a directive of the local government, or that the guarantor no longer has assets to bear the guarantee liability, and the guarantor should not be relieved of guarantee liability on this ground. Even if the guarantee contract in this case was entered into under a government directive, the guarantee liability cannot be waived. Water Supply Company is a legal person enterprise, not a "public institution for public interest purposes," and meets the qualifications as a guarantor. This case is a civil dispute, and Water Supply Company has no evidence of economic crimes. Hong Kong Shunkai (Group) Co., Ltd. is not a necessary joint defendant in this case. The first instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. It requested the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

This Court affirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

This Court holds: The loan contract signed between ICBC Wusi Sub-branch and Heshun Company in this case represented the true intentions of both parties and did not violate prohibitive provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and should be valid. The borrower Heshun Company failed to fully perform its contractual obligations after the contract matured and should bear civil liability for repaying the loan principal and interest to ICBC Wusi Sub-branch in accordance with the law. Water Supply Company entered into a written guarantee contract with ICBC Wusi Sub-branch, expressly undertaking to provide joint and several guarantee for the above loan of Heshun Company. Now that Heshun Company has failed to repay the debt at maturity, the guarantor Water Supply Company shall bear joint and several liability to ICBC Wusi Sub-branch for the above debt. Water Supply Company, as a legal person with full civil capacity, shall independently bear civil liability for its civil legal acts in accordance with the law. Water Supply Company's appeal ground that its guarantee was made under the administrative directives of the local government should exempt it from bearing guarantee liability to ICBC Wusi Sub-branch cannot be sustained. Because the guarantee contract in this case was entered into between Water Supply Company and ICBC Wusi Sub-branch, and Water Supply Company has no evidence that ICBC Wusi Sub-branch used fraud, duress, or other means when entering into the guarantee contract with it. The question of whether Water Supply Company was influenced by a third party outside the contract does not involve the rights and obligations between the parties to the contract. Since one party to a contract has no obligation to understand factors other than the counterparty's contracting behavior, it would be unfair to the guaranteed party ICBC Wusi Sub-branch for Water Supply Company to admit that it affixed its seal to the guarantee contract in this case while denying that the act of signing represented its true intention. A guarantee contract should not be deemed invalid solely because the guarantor's guarantee was made under a local government directive. Water Supply Company holds a business license for a legal person enterprise and is a for-profit enterprise legal person. Although its business operations have certain public service characteristics, it is not a public institution for public interest purposes. Water Supply Company's appeal contention that it does not meet the qualifications as a guarantor lacks factual basis, and this Court does not support it. The first instance judgment's finding that the guarantee contract in this case should be valid and that Water Supply Company should bear joint and several liability is not improper, and this Court should uphold it. Water Supply Company's appeal contention that this case may involve economic crimes and should be stayed lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it in accordance with the law. The question of whether the shareholder of the borrower Heshun Company has fully paid its registered capital does not have a direct legal relationship with the loan guarantee dispute in this case. Water Supply Company's appeal ground that Heshun Company's shareholder should be added to participate in this lawsuit lacks legal basis, and this Court does not support it in accordance with the law.

In summary, the first instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. This Court, in accordance with the provisions of Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, enters the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 160,098 shall be borne by Changle City Water Supply Company.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jiang Wei

Acting Judge: Chen Bailing

Acting Judge: Yang Zhengyu

March 11, 2005

Clerk: Yuan Hongxia
